speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your son's condition, could you describe the nature of his feeding difficulties and when you first noticed the abdominal distension?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and have you noticed any vomiting, particularly if it is green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the stool history, as "no diarrhea" is not specific; has the baby passed any meconium or regular stool in the last 24 hours, and was the initial meconium passed within the first 48 hours of life? I will also examine the perineum to check for an anal fissure or malformation.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

I need to see if there is evidence of bowel obstruction or the "double bubble" sign to differentiate between conditions like duodenal atresia or Hirschsprung disease. Please also check for any history of delayed meconium passage beyond 48 hours after birth.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings suggest a functional obstruction, likely Hirschsprung disease. Has the infant experienced any explosive stools or abdominal distension relief following rectal examinations in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will perform a digital rectal exam to assess for a tight anal sphincter and the absence of stool in the rectal vault. I also need to know if the baby passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the baby pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and did you observe any explosive expulsion of stool or gas following a rectal examination? I am looking for signs of a transition zone typical of Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now perform a digital rectal examination to feel for a tight sphincter and empty rectal vault, which are classic signs of Hirschsprung disease. Please also confirm definitively if the baby passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life, as delayed passage strongly supports this diagnosis.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Rectal Biopsy

I am proceeding with a suction rectal biopsy to confirm the absence of ganglion cells, which is diagnostic for Hirschsprung disease. Given the clinical presentation and X-ray findings, this is the definitive next step.
